market_context: The S&P 500 is down about 1.3% and trading near its session lows, below its 200-day moving average. Anthropic's record IPO triggered profit-taking in AI names, and every rally attempt this week (Nvidia earnings, the IPO open) has been sold. The 10-year yield is about 5.05% with a December Fed hike largely priced in, VIX is up to the high 20s, and small caps and health insurers are weak.

predictions.reasoning: Opening gains have faded on each of the last several days, and the S&P is now below its 200-day average, which puts trend followers on the sell side. VIX is rising and the 10-year is above 5% with a December hike priced in. Price is close to the day low of 717.55, so I expect only a small further drift lower into the close.

Small caps are rate-sensitive, and the 10-year is above 5% with a Fed hike expected in December. The Russell 2000 was the weakest index at midday, down roughly 2%, and it has not joined any of the bounce attempts. There is no catalyst for a late reversal.

NVDA is down about 10.6% over five days and sits near its day low of 147.82, after a post-earnings reversal that left it unusually oversold. A small mean-reversion bounce is possible into the close, but leadership uncertainty and ongoing downgrades cap the upside, so this is close to a coin flip.
